name: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel
route_note: Single IV infusion after lymphodepleting chemotherapy

discovery.note: Lentiviral CAR with two BCMA-binding single-domain (VHH) antibodies, a 4-1BB costimulatory domain and CD3ζ.

tagline: BCMA CAR T therapy with deep, durable responses in relapsed multiple myeloma
summary: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel is a CAR T-cell therapy directed at B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) on myeloma cells. Its unusual receptor carries two camelid-derived single-domain binders, and it produces very high response rates in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, including after one prior line in lenalidomide-refractory disease.
mechanism: Patient T cells are transduced with a lentiviral vector encoding a CAR whose antigen-binding part consists of two VHH domains targeting different BCMA epitopes, linked to 4-1BB and CD3ζ signalling domains.
After infusion, CAR T cells expand, recognise BCMA (TNFRSF17) on malignant plasma cells and kill them; normal plasma cells are also eliminated, leading to hypogammaglobulinaemia.
uses: Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after at least one prior line including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent, in lenalidomide-refractory disease

history.title: Chinese data and Janssen deal
history.detail: Legend presents early results of LCAR-B38M in China and partners with Janssen.

history.title: CARTITUDE-1
history.detail: Phase 1b/2 results show an overall response rate of about 97% in heavily pretreated myeloma.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in February for myeloma after four or more prior lines; EU conditional approval follows in May.

history.title: CARTITUDE-4
history.detail: Superior progression-free survival versus standard regimens after one to three prior lines.

history.title: Earlier-line approval
history.detail: FDA approves use after one prior line in lenalidomide-refractory myeloma.

history.title: Secondary malignancy warning
history.detail: A class boxed warning on T-cell malignancies is added in April 2024; in July 2024 CARTITUDE-4 reports a significant overall survival benefit.

pk.half_life: CAR transgene peaks ~2 weeks after infusion and persists for months
pk.metabolism: In vivo expansion and contraction of cells

safety.boxed_warning: Cytokine release syndrome, neurological toxicities (including ICANS, parkinsonism and Guillain–Barré syndrome), HLH/MAS, prolonged cytopenia and secondary haematological malignancies.

facts: Its CAR uses two llama-derived VHH binding domains rather than a conventional scFv.
Delayed movement and neurocognitive toxicity resembling parkinsonism is a distinctive adverse effect of BCMA CAR T therapy.
